case_title: Darshan Singh v. State of Punjab
accused_occupation: Servant (accused Darshan Singh, employed at the house of accused Avtar Singh); other accused's occupation not stated
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (mother of accused Avtar Singh; accused Swaran Kaur is his wife and accused Jagmohan Singh his son); Darshan Singh was a servant in Avtar Singh's house; prior dispute over unpaid lease money for inherited land
statutory_provisions: Penal Code 1860 s.302 (other sections not stated)
weapon: Dupatta (ligature around neck); folding iron chair (kursi) used as a blow; acid poured on the face; aluminium phosphide insecticide detected in the body
evidence_type: Extra-judicial confession; medical (postmortem and chemical examination); recovery (acid bottle, folding chair, motorcycle); circumstantial (motive, conduct after death, last-seen sighting); identification of body by clothing
confession: Extra-judicial confession made before PW-16 by accused Swaran Kaur, Jagmohan Singh and Darshan Singh, describing the dupatta, chair blow and acid; relied on by the trial court and the High Court, and the Supreme Court relied on it for Darshan Singh, supported by medical evidence and recovery of the chair
aggravating_circumstances: Face disfigured by acid poured with intention to avoid identification; accused not available in the village after the death and did not attend cremation or prayer ceremony
trial_court_outcome: Convicted Jagmohan Singh, Swaran Kaur and Darshan Singh; acquitted Avtar Singh; sentence not stated
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction upheld (Criminal Appeal No. 612-DB of 2007, judgment dated 19.02.2009)
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302) as charged; accused Swaran Kaur died during the appeal
neutral_facts: A decomposed body was found inside a jute bag in a field beside a bypass road, with maggots around it. The face had been disfigured by acid, so the body was identified only from its clothing by two sons-in-law of the victim. A dupatta was wrapped around the neck with two turns. The postmortem found a fracture of the hyoid bone, an irregular wound over the left chest, and fractures of the sixth and seventh ribs. The chemical examination detected aluminium phosphide insecticide in intestinal samples and phosphine in decomposed organs. A small telephone diary was found in the undershirt pocket of the body. A witness reported seeing a man and a woman on a TVS motorcycle at about 5:30 am on 22 March 2005 carrying a gunny bag; he could not identify either person. The victim had inherited land from a deceased son and leased part of it to the accused for a yearly rent, but the lease money was not paid, and the victim complained of this to a village sarpanch. After the body was identified, police could not trace the accused in the village. Later, a witness stated that one accused had confessed to him in detail, describing a dupatta, a blow with a chair and acid poured on the face. A bottle of acid was recovered from a house on the basis of a disclosure, a folding iron chair was recovered from another house, and a motorcycle was recovered.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; face disfigured by acid; fracture of hyoid bone; irregular wound over left chest; fractures of 6th and 7th ribs; aluminium phosphide poisoning noted in postmortem opinion
number_of_offences: 1 charged (murder, IPC s.302 per headnote; separate charges not listed); 1 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Unpaid lease money for the victim's land (lease at Rs.4,000 per bigha; only Rs.1,000 paid)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation finding stated; court found acid was poured with intention to avoid identification of the body
motive: Dispute over lease money for land the victim inherited from her deceased son; accused Avtar Singh had not paid the lease, which the court accepted
key_evidence_accepted: Extra-judicial confession before PW-16 (for Darshan Singh) corroborated by postmortem findings and recovery of the folding chair; postmortem findings of hyoid fracture and two dupatta turns; recovery of acid bottle on disclosure; photographs showing acid disfigurement; lease dispute and PW-11 and PW-13 evidence; absence from village and non-attendance at cremation; last-seen sighting of a man and woman on a TVS motorcycle
witness_credibility: Court accepted PW-11 (Sarpanch) and PW-13 (son-in-law) on lease dispute and absence of accused; PW-14 could not identify accused but his sighting of a man and woman on a TVS motorcycle was held relevant; the court did not separately assess PW-16's reliability beyond corroboration by medical evidence and recovery
post_offence_conduct: Accused not found in the village after the occurrence; did not attend cremation or the prayer ceremony held after one week; acid bottle concealed in house and recovered on disclosure; folding chair concealed in house and recovered on disclosure; motorcycle concealed and recovered
bail_history: Accused Swaran Kaur released on bail by the Supreme Court on 4 October 2010; no other bail details stated
trial_duration: offence: not given (last seen 22 March 2005; FIR 28 March 2005); trial judgment: 23 May 2007 / 26 May 2007; High Court: 19 February 2009; Supreme Court: 06 December 2019
legal_representation: Accused (appellants): D. P. Singh, Ms. Sonam Gupta, Ms. Ishita Jain, Sanjay Jain, Advocates. State: Ms. Jaspreet Gogia, Ms. Mandakini Singh, Ms. Ashima Mandla, Ms. Anupriya, Advocates
investigation_status: FIR lodged 28 March 2005; body recovered and postmortem done; arrests and recoveries made; investigation completed and accused sent for trial (charge sheet not expressly mentioned)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted Jagmohan Singh, Swaran Kaur and Darshan Singh, acquitted Avtar Singh. High Court: appeals dismissed, 19 February 2009. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed; Swaran Kaur died during pendency; Darshan Singh and Jagmohan Singh to surrender
prosecution_argument: Last-seen evidence of a man and woman on a TVS motorcycle is relevant even without identification; motive was proved through the Sarpanch and the son-in-law; extra-judicial confession need not always be corroborated (Ram Lal)
defence_argument: Chain of circumstances incomplete; last-seen evidence rejected; extra-judicial confession is weak evidence; no motive attributable to the accused; poison not administered or recovered and inconsistent with strangulation; hyoid fracture does not necessarily mean strangulation
legal_principle_applied: Chain of circumstances test; extra-judicial confession may support conviction, with corroboration by medical or recovery evidence; post-offence conduct and motive as circumstances
precedent_relied_upon: Ram Lal v. State of Himachal Pradesh (2018 SCC OnLine SC 1730), quoted by the court; Ajay Singh v. State of Maharashtra (2007) 12 SCC 341, S. Arul Raja v. State of Tamil Nadu (2010) 8 SCC 233, Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116 and Devi Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2019 SCC OnLine 39) referred to in arguments
judicial_aggravating_factors: Acid disfigurement of the body to avoid identification; accused's absence from the village and non-attendance at cremation and prayer ceremony
other_sentence_order: Darshan Singh and Jagmohan Singh directed to surrender to undergo the remaining sentence
